Summary: A capitalized sentence-opening word ('Across', 'Between', 'Within', 'Given', 'Overall') is selected as the question's subject, so the named entity is never resolved
Description: 1) Original intent: the Query Contract (KRYL-1372) selects THE subject of a question once and the registry/SEC admission path (KRYL-1380) resolves it; the subject of 'Across all six domains, what formation exists around Oracle?' is Oracle. 2) Acceptance criteria: (a) a capital letter carried only by position (the first word of a sentence or clause) is not evidence of a name: a closed-class opener (preposition, conjunction, determiner, adverb, pronoun) at the start of a sentence is never a name run, whether or not the question has a recognised interrogative stem; (b) C07 and C11 ('Across all six domains, what formation exists around Oracle/Tesla?') select and resolve Oracle and Tesla, with the selection rule recorded; (c) adjacent patterns resolve the same way: 'Between ownership and capital, how is Boeing connected?', 'Within the last year, what changed around Verizon?', 'Overall, what relationships exist around Intel?', 'Given the filings, what is forming around Netflix?'; (d) an opener-only question with no named entity ('Across all six domains, what formation exists?') yields no subject and is classified as before; (e) a sentence-initial unregistered name that is a name ('Daytona raises $5M', 'Anduril ...', 'Integrated Biosciences ...') is still selected as before (LEAD_NAME / EXPLICIT_IN_QUESTION); (f) the existing query-contract and subject-scope suites stay green; the full benchmark is not rerun. 3) Current implementation state: defect reproduced on Dev 2026-10-11 (C07, C11 captured in specs/benchmark/milestone1: 'Subject selected: Across', no structure attributed). Cause traced: subjectScope -> buildQueryContract; a question with no recognised interrogative stem is not split, so namedRuns() reads the sentence-initial 'Across' as a Title-Case name and it becomes the LEAD_NAME subject. Separately traced (not fixed by this ticket): a plain name whose SEC lookup returns only look-alike registrants ('Ford' returns ABS trusts inside the 100-hit window; 'Ford Motor' verifies as FORD MOTOR CO) and misspellings ('Frod', 'Tesle') find no registrant because the filing-index search is lexical; both need a name source decision. 4) Dependencies: KRYL-1372 (query contract), KRYL-1380 (SEC filer admission). 5) Superseded by a newer ticket: no. 6) Maps to the current product model: yes (subject first, then analysis). Status: opened and in progress 2026-10-11.
